name: Loops over every Space in the target row vs. no traversal at all (single hard-coded space)
side_a: no_deduct — the answer contains an actual traversal of the row (indexed `for` over `board[targetRow].length` or enhanced `for (Space s : board[targetRow])`) that touches each Space to accumulate points and/or test color; credit even if the accumulation is buggy (resetting `sum`, early `return`, off-by-one seed).
side_b: deduct — the answer never iterates the row: it reads a single hard-coded element (e.g. `board[0][0]`) and immediately branches on an uninitialized/never-updated flag, so no row-wide points sum or color check is ever performed.

name: color comparison uses equals() vs. uses ==/!= reference comparison
side_a: Do not deduct when the two color values are compared with the equals() method (e.g., `!currentSpace.getColor().equals(firstColor)`), since the sub-item requires a non-reference String comparison.
side_b: Deduct when the colors are compared with the reference operators == or != (e.g., `if (s.getColor() != firstColor)`), even though getColor() is correctly called on a Space and the rest of the logic is right; a reference comparison is not a correct color comparison.

name: a color comparison exists somewhere in the code vs. no color comparison is attempted
side_a: Do not deduct when the code actually contains a comparison of color values anywhere in the method (even inside a loop, early-return, or flag assignment).
side_b: Deduct when the response never calls a color method or compares colors at all — it merely declares/uses a flag such as `boolean allSameColor = true;` without any getColor() call — since there is nothing to earn the color-comparison point.

name: Point value must be fetched and added inside the loop body vs. fetching it once in the variable's initializer counts as both init and accumulation
side_a: Deduct when the only call to the point method sits in the declaration/initializer of the points variable (`int sum = board[0][0].getPoints();`) and nothing is ever added to that variable afterwards — there is no separate initialization step and no accumulation step, so the response neither properly initializes a points accumulator nor accumulates retrieved values. Credit only when the variable is first given a seed value and point values are then fetched from spaces and combined into it inside a loop body.
side_b: Do not deduct: the response declares and initializes a points variable and calls the point method on a space, which satisfies the two hard requirements; obtaining the value directly in the initializer is merely an incorrect/incomplete sum, which the rubric forgives.

name: Partial/early-terminated traversal of the row still credits vs. the loop must sum every space in the row
side_a: Do not deduct when the loop may stop early and therefore sums only part of the row (e.g., a `return` inside the loop body), or when the running total is reset/seeded wrongly; as long as some loop iteration adds a retrieved point value to the initialized variable, the incomplete total is just an 'incorrect sum'.
side_b: Deduct whenever the code cannot sum all spaces of the target row — an early `return` inside the loop, a reset of the accumulator each iteration, or a nonzero seed means no genuine row total is ever produced.

name: Defects in the point-sum accumulation (wrong initializer, sum reset inside the loop): ignored here vs. counted as failing to 'access all spaces'
side_a: No deduct for errors in how the running point total is built, as long as the loop visits every space of the row and compares each space's color to the reference color. A wrong sum seed (e.g., `int sum = 1;`) or a reset of the accumulator inside the loop body (`sum = 0;` before adding) is charged under the summation sub-item, not this one — the color traversal is still complete.
side_b: Deduct whenever the loop body fails to correctly accumulate each space's points, on the theory that a space whose points are discarded (sum reset each iteration) or a total polluted by a bogus seed means the response did not truly 'access all the spaces in the row'.

name: running-total accumulator is initialized to 0 once and only ever added to vs the total is seeded non-zero, reset inside the loop, or never accumulated at all
side_a: Award the sub-item when the response declares a single total initialized to zero before the loop and only ever does `sum += space.getPoints()` inside the loop, so the returned value is the true sum of every visited space's points (possibly doubled).
side_b: Deduct when the accumulator itself is broken independently of any color/bounds issue — it is seeded with a non-zero constant, is re-assigned/zeroed inside the loop body so earlier additions are lost, or there is no iteration at all and only one hard-coded space's points are used. This is 'computing the sum incorrectly' and is not covered by the same-color or bounds allowances.

name: full traversal of the row before returning vs returning early mid-loop on a color mismatch, truncating the sum
side_a: Award the sub-item when the loop visits every space in the target row before any return, so the color decision only selects between sum and 2*sum of a complete total.
side_b: Deduct when the method returns from inside the summation loop as soon as a color mismatch is found, so the value returned is a partial sum of only the spaces seen so far rather than the whole row's points; the 'incorrectly determine same color' allowance covers picking the wrong branch, not stopping the summation.
